notes.text: Peru's credit system has largely de-dollarised: foreign-currency loans fell from 46.5% of total credit in 2010 to 24.6% in 2023, helped by repo operations and higher reserve requirements on foreign-currency funding after 2013, though the IMF finds the trend has stalled since 2022. A lower dollar share limits households' exposure to sol depreciation, although the IMF judges remaining unhedged dollar credit riskier and recommends targeted macroprudential measures.

sources.title: Peru: 2025 Article IV Consultation, Staff Report (IMF Country Report No. 25/125)

notes.text: Mortgage borrowers under Fondo MiVivienda's Nuevo Crédito MiVivienda can receive a non-repayable Bono del Buen Pagador on homes valued from S/ 69,900 to S/ 367,600, worth S/ 27,800 in the lowest band and S/ 7,900 in the highest under DS 011-2026-VIVIENDA, with larger amounts for certified sustainable homes and none above S/ 367,600. Because the grant shrinks as home values rise and the bands are indexed each year to Lima consumer prices, it concentrates extra purchasing power in the lower and middle price bands.

Techo Propio, the housing ministry's social-housing programme run through Fondo MiVivienda, gives households earning up to S/ 3,715 a month a non-repayable Bono Familiar Habitacional, conditional on prior saving, to buy new homes priced up to S/ 136,100. The grant adds to buyers' purchasing power at the bottom of the market and so supports demand for low-cost new housing.
